hook: Renée Richardson Gosline is a senior lecturer and principal research scientist at MIT Sloan and head of the Human-First AI group at MIT's Initiative on the Digital Economy. Her argument runs against the grain of most enterprise AI work: frictionlessness is treated as the goal, and she has shown that removing friction from an AI system can erode the judgement the system was meant to support. She distinguishes bad friction, which should be audited out, from beneficial friction, which should be designed in, and her forthcoming book In Praise of Friction makes the case at length. She took her AB in sociology, an MA, and a PhD in marketing and consumer behaviour, all at Harvard, and worked at Moët Hennessy and Leo Burnett before academia.

quick_facts: Senior Lecturer and Principal Research Scientist at MIT Sloan since 2018, and Assistant Professor there from 2009 to 2018
Heads the Human-First AI group at MIT's Initiative on the Digital Economy
Digital Fellow at Stanford's Digital Economy Lab since 2020
Named to the Thinkers50 Radar list and to Poets and Quants' World's Top 40 Professors under 40
AB in Sociology with Honors, MA in Sociology, and PhD in Marketing and Consumer Behavior, all from Harvard
Has presented her research to the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy and to the OECD
Has collaborated with Goldman Sachs, Salesforce, IBM, Procter and Gamble, Accenture, Johnson and Johnson and Capgemini
Serves on the boards of the National Kidney Foundation, The Equity Alliance Fund, the 4As CX Council and the advisory board of Sloan Management Review

achievements.title: The beneficial friction thesis
achievements.impact: Distinguishes bad friction, which should be audited out of a process, from beneficial friction, which should be designed in. Research with the Commonwealth Bank of Australia found that asking people to articulate why they were following an AI agent's recommendation reduced uncritical reliance and improved accuracy, without a significant increase in time spent.

achievements.title: Friction auditing
achievements.impact: Pioneered the practice of auditing AI-mediated decision processes for where friction has been removed and where it should be restored, aimed at minimising harm rather than maximising speed.

achievements.title: In Praise of Friction
achievements.impact: Forthcoming book from MIT Press setting out a research-backed plan for human-first AI systems.

achievements.title: Research on algorithmic aversion and human favouritism
achievements.impact: Experimental work on when people abandon AI after seeing it err, how cognitive style predicts preference for AI over human input, and how people judge content from AI, human experts and human-AI collaboration.

achievements.title: Co-founder, MIT Sloan Behavioral Research Lab
achievements.impact: Co-founded the B-Lab, the experimental facility supporting behavioural research at MIT Sloan.
